title: Point-wise Anomaly Detection via Fold-bifurcation ODE
claim: Prior detectors capture only instantaneous error spikes; ours accumulates stress through dynamics, so the whole anomalous span is detected.
layout: 2 side-by-side boxed panels, top-to-bottom flow, gray vs blue borders, ODE equation in center
description: Two side-by-side boxed panels. The left, gray-bordered panel is titled 'Prediction-based Anomaly Detection'. It flows down from a green input time series with a pink abnormal region, through a gray 'Forecasting Model' box, to an anomaly-score plot. That plot has one sharp spike with only a narrow orange detected sliver, and a red dashed threshold line. A thick black arrow leads from the forecasting model into the right panel. The right panel has a blue border and is titled 'FOLD: point-wise Anomaly Detection'. It flows down through navy stress-signal curves (circled in red), a light-blue box with the fold-bifurcation ODE dz/dt = αS(t) − βz² − γz, and a final anomaly score. In that score the whole pink region is covered in orange and the curve crosses the red threshold line. Circles and arrows call out the contrast between sudden stress and state transition.
caption: Contrasting conventional predictionbased anomaly detection with our proposed FOLD. While prediction-based models capture only instantaneous error spikes (sudden stress), FOLD extracts sensitivity–uncertainty stress signals and integrates them via fold-bifurcation dynamics, modeling how stress accumulates into state transitions. This enables accurate and interpretable point-wise anomaly detection.
abstract: Anomaly detection in time series is essential for applications from industrial monitoring to financial risk management. Recent methods --- including forecasting error models, representation learning, augmentation, and weak-label learning --- have achieved strong results for specific anomaly types such as sudden point or gradual collective anomalies. While many prior works report window-level metrics that may mask errors, several recent methods evaluate at the point level as well. Our goal is to use a stricter point-wise protocol to make masking effects explicit. We introduce FOLD (Point-wise Anomaly Detection via fold-bifurcation), a framework that reframes detection as tracking a system’s proximity to a critical transition. FOLD extracts stress signals from a forecasting model and integrates them with a fold-bifurcation inspired ODE to produce the risk state, flagging anomalies once it crosses a threshold calibrated on normal data. This requires no anomaly labels and no additional detector training, enabling a parameter-free and efficient detection process. By modeling anomalies as stress accumulation toward a tipping point, FOLD naturally aligns with point-wise detection, providing a unifying and interpretable perspective that complements type-specific methods. Experiments on 40 benchmarks against 34 state-of-the-art baselines show that FOLD achieves competitive or superior performance, with particular strength under strict point-wise evaluation.
